sample_unit: retrospective MRI cases read by 16 radiologists

links.outcome: Radiologist diagnostic accuracy (AUC) for ARIA detection with versus without AI assistance
links.effect: Assisted AUC 0.87 for ARIA-E (improvement 0.05, 95% CI 0.02-0.08; P=.001) and 0.83 for ARIA-H (improvement 0.04, 95% CI 0.02-0.07; P=.001). Sensitivity 87% vs 71% (ARIA-E), 79% vs 69% (ARIA-H).
links.quote: Radiologists assisted by the software were significantly superior in detecting ARIA than unassisted radiologists, with a mean assisted AUC of 0.87 (95% CI, 0.84-0.91) for ARIA-E detection (AUC improvement of 0.05 [95% CI, 0.02-0.08]; P = .001]) and 0.83 (95% CI, 0.78-0.87) for ARIA-H detection (AUC improvement of 0.04 [95% CI, 0.02-0.07]; P = .001).

screen.reason: The study uses a multiple-reader multiple-case design comparing radiologists' performance with versus without an AI-assistive software tool for detecting ARIA.

primary.practice: AI-assisted radiologist reading versus unassisted reading
